raw: 22.1 CI Definition, Scope, Relationship to Intelligence[^12]
teaching_note: Counterintelligence examines threats to information and institutional integrity; routine security administration and criminal adjudication answer different questions. The cited non-state-actor overview is context, not a general legal mandate. Define a lawful protective purpose before considering records; learners do not investigate people, infer disloyalty or convert protected disclosures and lawful association into suspicion.
title: CI Definition, Scope, Relationship to Intelligence

teaching_note: These labels describe different institutional approaches, not permissions granted to a class. Restrict the exercise to defensive assessment of supplied artifacts and protected reporting: no penetration, covert contact, deception, monitoring of colleagues or investigative expansion. A justified protective step can coexist with unresolved attribution.
title: Offensive vs. Defensive Counterintelligence

raw: 22.3 Insider Threat Analysis: Critical Thinking Techniques (CDSE)[^108]
teaching_note: Completed offline case: L1 is a synthetic access log showing an out-of-hours file opening; L2 is an approved maintenance ticket for that time; L3 is a clock-offset notice; no record shows copying or disclosure. The filled judgment is access anomaly observed (L1), possible authorization (L2), timing unreliable (L3), and misconduct unsupported; compare maintenance, account compromise and clock error without scoring a person's motives. Withheld L4 confirms the ticket covers this file, so close the alleged unauthorized-access claim, correct the minimized report and retain only the authorized process record. A remaining account-control question belongs to the designated protective function, not learner investigation (see [@sec:analytic-workflow]; [@ageint108]).
title: Insider Threat Analysis: Critical Thinking Techniques (CDSE)

teaching_note: A human agent in a historical account is not an AI software agent. Reports attributed to several intermediaries may depend on the same controlled origin; map that dependence before treating apparent agreement as corroboration. Discuss uncertainty and retrospective source claims, not recruitment, handling, deception or tests of loyalty; the inherited overview and uploaded material do not establish any particular operation.
title: Historical double-agent claims: dependence and verification

teaching_note: The source standards here support analytic discipline, not a history or instructions for penetration. Distinguish claimed access from independently corroborated information and from demonstrated control; apparent insider knowledge can also come from public records or shared sources. Hold the historical claim when operation-specific evidence is absent; do not emulate tradecraft [@ageint297].
title: Historical penetration claims: evidentiary and authority limits

raw: 22.6 Polygraph: Use and Limitations in CI
teaching_note: Physiological responses are not uniquely deception; distinguish specific-event testing from broad screening and do not infer guilt from a positive screen. The National Research Council's 2003 executive summary cautions against generalizing specific-incident research to screening and documents serious screening limits (https://www.nationalacademies.org/read/10420/chapter/2); ICD 203 is not polygraph-validity evidence. For a separate hypothetical arithmetic exercise, assume 1,000 cases, 10 true target events, sensitivity 80% and specificity 90%: TP=8, FN=2, FP=99, TN=891, so only 8/107 positive screens are true positives. These assumed rates are not measured polygraph performance; the defensible answer is no adverse-person conclusion and no learner testing or evasion instruction.
title: Polygraph: Use and Limitations in CI

teaching_note: Potential access, actual access, copying, disclosure and resulting harm are separate propositions. A damage assessment should bound affected records and uncertainty without presuming a guilty actor; remediation may protect a system while attribution remains unknown. Minimize personal data, use authorized reporting and preserve exculpatory corrections; the cited analytic standards do not authorize investigative activity [@ageint297].
title: Damage Assessment and Control

raw: 22.8 Case Studies: Hanssen, Ames, Lee, Pollard
teaching_note: The inherited surname 'Lee' is insufficiently specified, and these generic standards do not establish facts about any named case; do not guess the identity or equate accusation, charge, plea, conviction and exoneration. A defensible comparison needs a dated primary record for each claimed event, what was knowable then, and later corrections. Until supplied, those case-specific cells remain unknown rather than turning a list of names into a typology of guilt.
title: Named case comparisons: identity, adjudication and hindsight limits
